messages:
Prasanna: Heads up — noticed a reproducible token divergence when bringing up the new int8-medium-x model with long prefix priming. Steps to repro below.

Prasanna: Repro summary: run a 5k token prompt split into 1k prefix + 4k continuation, with kvcache_stride=16 during priming. After passing the 2048 boundary the output tokens start to mismatch against fp16 baseline (diff shows ~0.7% token drift by token 2600).

Prasanna: Minimal command we used:
```
./serve_local --model int8-medium-x --quantize int8 --kv-stride 16 --prefill 1000 --max-tokens 5000 --seed 42
```
Output snippet: first 2048 tokens identical, then at token 2053 fp16: "the committee decided" vs int8: "the committe decided" (typo, then later grows).

Dina: ugh. did you try running with --kv-checksum and compare checksums after each prefill chunk? that helps isolate if it's an index/offseting issue vs quant kernel error. :thinking:

Prasanna: yep ran with --kv-checksum. Checksums diverge right after the 2048->2049 stride boundary. CRC matches up to chunk N, then flips. so it's likely an off-by-one when we compact kv blocks or when we write rotated RoPE indices.

Jonah: can you paste the kv-checksum log? also what runtime flags for batch alignment / continuous-batching? some of the int8 kernels assume 32-byte alignment and we had fallback paths that tile-copy and can drop a row accidentally.

Prasanna: pasted a tiny excerpt:
```
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] prefill-chunk-0 crc=ab12ef
[2026-03-10T14:02:12Z] prefill-chunk-1 crc=ab12ef
[2026-03-10T14:02:15Z] prefill-chunk-2 crc=ab12ef
[2026-03-10T14:02:18Z] prefill-chunk-3 crc=cd34be  <-- divergence
```
chunk-3 starts at token 2049.

Maia: interesting. is this specific to stride=16? try stride=8 and stride=32. if it's stride-sensitive maybe our roaming compaction logic (kv_compact_stride) miscomputes starting index when stride doesn't divide the block size evenly.

Prasanna: quick local results: stride=8 -> no divergence up to 5k. stride=32 -> divergence earlier (token ~1800). stride=1 -> no divergence. so definitely stride-dependent.

Jonah: ok that points at the compaction math. @ops-bot can you run the kernel fuzz job (int8-kv-compact) against this seed 42 prefills (1k chunks) and capture memory copy paths + alignment branch taken counts? want to see if we hit the memcpy fallback.

ops-bot: scheduled job int8-kv-compact/1949993333-fuzz-seed42 on queue gpu-qa-2. logs will post here when done. ETA ~ 8m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Dina: while we wait, two quick suggestions: 1) add an assert in the compaction routine that (start_index % stride) == 0 for the expected branch; 2) rerun with ropenorm=false to see if rotary scaling interacts (we had a historical bug where ropenorm + compact produced a 1-off).

Prasanna: I can try the ropenorm toggle now. Also will capture nvprof of the memcpy branch.

Maia: if this is only hitting quantized path, consider a patch to duplicate the compaction index calc from fp16 path (cheap but safe) and test perf impact. If it fixes, we can iterate a better optimized math later.

Prasanna: created a quick branch prasanna/kv-stride-fix with the assert and fp16-copy fallback. running CI smoke now. will update when ops-bot posts fuzz results. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: fuzz job finished. Summary: memcpy-fallback taken in 73% of runs where stride % 16 != 0; CUDA kernel path taken otherwise. reproducer failures correlate with memcpy path, and heap-check flagged an uninitialized tail word in 12 runs. attaching logs to the ticket: https://redwood-internal/issue/ML-1347

Jonah: that nails it — memcpy path had a tail-copy bug. thanks ops-bot. Prasanna, once your CI passes, let's run full regression against the RTT eval set and the LRM benchmarks (5 seeds) to measure quality delta and perf hit. if fallback fixes correctness we can look at optimizing memcpy routine.

Prasanna: will do. initial smoke on branch shows correctness restored for stride=16 and 32. perf hit ~+4% latency in worst-case memcopy runs. I'll open an RFC for a targeted memcpy rewrite and include perf profiles.

Dina: awesome. add a small test in longctx QA that exercises stride values 1,8,16,32 and asserts CRC parity with fp16 baseline up to 8k tokens. that should catch regressions early.

Prasanna: added tests to PR. cc @Maia @Jonah for review. thanks all.
